1	# Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan - 2026-05-31
2	
3	## Bottom Line
4	
5	The intended user experience is simple: Dock shows a flat, newest-first list of the work that most recently happened. Manual pins may keep a thread visible, but they must not invent recency, status, title, summary, or activity.
6	
7	The implementation path is also simple at the architectural level: make the relay card projection the single semantic owner. Swift renders the card stream. It does not repair, reorder, or re-source card truth.
8	
9	Related audit: [Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit](CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md).
10	
11	## Model Consensus
12	
13	This plan was built from the requested parallel model-consensus run:
14	
15	- Model A: `claude-opus-4-8`, effort `max`.
16	- Model B: `gpt-5.5`, effort `high`.
17	- Artifacts: `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-single-source-contract-20260531T183258Z/`.
18	
19	Consensus result:
20	
21	- One relay projection folds raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, live status, and session-index identity into one stored card.
22	- `DockThreadCardDTO` remains the app-facing card shape.
23	- `activityAtMs`, `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `displaySummary`, card `status`, and freshness are relay-owned card semantics.
24	- Swift becomes render-only for card truth.
25	- Card-truth side-door routes and tests are deleted or internalized.
26	- Ops-health endpoints stay, but they cannot be presented as data freshness.
27	
28	## Non-Negotiable Invariant
29	
30	Every Dock and Archive card's recency, ordering, summary, status, and freshness are computed once by the relay projection from a canonical per-thread activity timestamp.
31	
32	Canonical activity is:
33	
34	```text
35	max(thread.updatedAt, thread.createdAt, newest turn timestamp, live event timestamp)
36	```
37	
38	The relay persists that activity and derives `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `activityAtMs`, `displaySummary`, `status`, and `freshness` from it. Swift consumes only the `dock/*` and `archive/*` card streams for card list truth.
39	
40	## Key Root Cause
41	
42	The current Dock path is shape-safe but source-unsafe:
43	
44	- Shape-safe: `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` generates `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift`.
45	- Source-unsafe: `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` and `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` can build cards from `thread/list` and `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while the newest work may exist only in `thread/turns/list`.
46	
47	That is how the app can show old work at the top while the latest work exists in the raw thread-turn data.
48	
49	## Canonical Owner
50	
51	Canonical card truth belongs here:
52	
53	- Projection/reconcile: `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`.
54	- Projection semantics: `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs`.
55	- Raw data folding: `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`.
56	- Stored card state: `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
57	- App-facing shape: `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
58	- Swift decoded shape: `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift`.
59	
60	The Swift client may format dates and render UI. It may filter/search/group visible rows. It must not compute card recency, card order, card status, card freshness, or card summary from another source.
61	
62	## Source Disposition
63	
64	| Source | Current role | Final role |
65	| --- | --- | --- |
66	| Raw `thread/list` | Dock/Archive row enumeration and stale timestamp source. | Internal relay input only. Never app-facing card proof. |
67	| Raw `thread/read` | Detail read and Dock enrichment with `includeTurns:false`. | Detail route stays app-facing. Relay card projection uses it internally for thread metadata. |
68	| Raw `thread/turns/list` | Thread Detail and oracle/audit paths; Dock does not use it for cards. | Detail route stays app-facing. Relay projection uses bounded latest-turn reads for card recency. |
69	| Raw `thread/search` | Diagnostic/oracle side door. | Remove app-facing relay route. Keep no card-proof tests on it. |
70	| Raw `thread/goal/get` | Diagnostic/oracle side door. | Remove app-facing relay route unless a non-card feature later owns it explicitly. |
71	| Raw `thread/loaded/list` | Live membership/status input. | Internal relay input only. No app-facing card proof. |
72	| `$CODEX_HOME/session_index.jsonl` | Can supplement rows with candidate metadata. | ID-only discovery input. Display fields come from canonical relay projection. |
73	| `threads` SQLite table | Stored card rows plus read-time live lease overlay. | Single stored card source. No read-time overlay mutates emitted card truth. |
74	| `live_leases` | Read-time status overlay. | Internal projection input; live status is folded before storage/emission. |
75	| `ThreadSummaryCache` | Wired relay-side summary helper/cache. | Absorb into canonical projection; keep only pure latest-safe-turn summary helper if needed. |
76	| Swift local metadata | Pins, labels, rails, and cached pinned display. | Pins, labels, rails, pin order only. No title/status/activity/summary fallback. |
77	| `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz` | Ops/transport health. | Keep. They are not card truth and must not be shown as data freshness. |
78	
79	## Endpoint Disposition
80	
81	| Endpoint / route | Final decision | Reason |
82	| --- | --- | --- |
83	| `dock/subscribe` | Keep | Primary active card stream. |
84	| `dock/update` | Keep | Primary active delta stream. |
85	| `dock/resync` | Keep | Primary active resync path. |
86	| `archive/subscribe` | Keep | Primary archive card stream. |
87	| `archive/update` | Keep | Primary archive delta stream. |
88	| `archive/resync` | Keep | Primary archive resync path. |
89	| `thread/read` | Keep | Thread Detail legitimately needs raw thread data. Not a Dock card list source. |
90	| `thread/turns/list` | Keep | Thread Detail legitimately needs turns. Relay projection also uses it internally. |
91	| `thread/resume` | Keep | Thread Detail live/resume path. |
92	| `thread/list` | Remove as app-facing route | Raw list is not card truth and is currently a stale side door. |
93	| `thread/search` | Remove as app-facing route | Search results cannot be a global card source. |
94	| `thread/goal/get` | Remove as app-facing card route | Goal data is not Dock card truth. |
95	| `thread/loaded/list` | Remove as app-facing route | Live membership is relay input, not app card truth. |
96	| `relay/state/snapshot` | Delete shipped route and tests | It is an oracle side door. Tests must prove through app card streams. |
97	| `state/query` | Delete shipped route and tests | It bypasses stream sequencing and trains tests on the wrong path. |
98	
99	## Implementation Plan
100	
101	### Phase 0: Add Canonical Relay Recency
102	
103	Add canonical recency without changing Swift yet.
104	
105	Changes:
106	
107	- Add one canonical card-row read/fold path in `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`, for example `readCanonicalDockThreadRows(...)`.
108	- In `reconcileDock`, after draining `thread/list`, fetch newest turn data only for:
109	  - live-leased threads
110	  - top-N visible/publish-window candidates
111	- Use `thread/turns/list` with `sortDirection: "desc"` and page size/concurrency constants in `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs`.
112	- Reuse existing turns-desc patterns from `scripts/dock-relay-state-snapshot.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`, and `scripts/dock-relay-probe.mjs`.
113	- Set canonical activity as `max(updatedAt, createdAt, newestTurn, liveEvent)`.
114	- Generalize the activity-derived Archive order key and use it for active Dock too.
115	- Stop using active Dock list ordinal `dockOrderKey(index, ...)` as semantic ordering.
116	- Add a stored canonical activity column in `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
117	- Fix `mergeAuthoritativeThreadRead(...)` so merging `thread/read includeTurns:false` cannot delete or downgrade newer turn activity.
118	
119	Tests:
120	
121	- New relay regression: stale `thread/read.updatedAt`, newer `thread/turns/list.startedAt`, card uses the newer turn for `activityAtMs`, `activityAt`, and `orderKey`.
122	- New relay ordering test: `listDockCards` order equals canonical activity order.
123	- Rewrite the old "activity from thread fields" assertions, including the old `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs` cases that assume no turn warming.
124	
125	Gate:
126	
127	```bash
128	rtk npm run test:relay
129	rtk npm run contract:check
130	```
131	
132	### Phase 1: Make Live Status Part Of Projection, Not A Read-Time Overlay
133	
134	The stored card row should already contain the live status that the client sees.
135	
136	Changes:
137	
138	- Remove read-time `applyLeaseToCard` mutation from `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
139	- Fold live status into canonical projection before `upsertThreadCard`.
140	- Lease acquisition, status change, and expiry must schedule recompute and delta publish.
141	- Keep lease status status-only: it must not mutate activity, order, summary, title, or freshness.
142	- Collapse `LiveStatusCache` plus `live_leases` into one source feeding `SessionRouter` and card projection.
143	- Absorb `ThreadSummaryCache` into the canonical projection. It is wired today, so do not delete it as "unused"; remove its construction site only when the canonical projection owns the equivalent behavior.
144	- Make session-index supplements ID-only.
145	- Change supplement validation so one bad supplemental candidate fails that candidate, not the entire host freshness.
146	
147	Tests:
148	
149	- Expired lease falls back to projected status and never leaves stale `running`.
150	- Lease status changes do not change activity, order, summary, or title.
151	- Live-only thread appears through canonical projection, not through a lease overlay.
152	- Session-index candidate can contribute an ID, but stale session-index `updatedAt` cannot win.
153	- Supplemental validation failure marks that candidate failed without poisoning all host freshness.
154	
155	Gate:
156	
157	```bash
158	rtk npm run test:relay
159	```
160	
161	### Phase 2: Tighten The Contract
162	
163	After the relay always emits canonical activity, make the schema enforce that clients receive it.
164	
165	Changes:
166	
167	- Make `activityAtMs` required in `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
168	- Regenerate `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` using the repo's contract generation path.
169	- Add fixtures under `contract/dock/fixtures/` for:
170	  - stale thread-level timestamp but newer turn timestamp
171	  - stale retained host freshness
172	  - live status projection
173	- Replace keyword-style confidence in `scripts/check-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs` with real JSON-Schema fixture validation.
174	
175	Gate:
176	
177	```bash
178	rtk npm run contract:check
179	```
180	
181	### Phase 3: Make Swift Render-Only For Card Truth
182	
183	Swift still owns presentation, but not semantic card truth.
184	
185	Changes:
186	
187	- In `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`, remove the `lastActivityDate`-first ordering workaround once relay `orderKey` is canonical.
188	- Sort card rows by relay `orderKey` for body rows and groups.
189	- Keep local search, filters, grouping, facets, counts, and relative-time formatting.
190	- In `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardRowProjector.swift`, consume required `activityAtMs` as the display date source; remove ISO fallback and `.distantPast` card-truth behavior.
191	- Delete `LocalPinnedDisplaySnapshot` / `lastKnownPinnedDisplay` as a card-data source.
192	- Render pinned-but-missing rows as explicitly not loaded while preserving label, rail, and pin order.
193	- Add first-class stale state in `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)`, `AppConnectivityStore`, and global status UI.
194	- `.stale` must not be online-like.
195	- Remove `thread/list` from app-critical health in `CodexDock/Diagnostics/ObservabilityContract.swift` and `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift`.
196	- Remove `AppServerClient.threadList` if no legitimate non-card production caller remains.
197	- Prefer one stream reducer: move Archive and cleanup away from loose collector behavior if it duplicates `ThreadCardTable`.
198	
199	Tests:
200	
201	- Rewrite `DockStoreTestsProjection.swift` ordering tests to assert Swift preserves relay `orderKey`.
202	- Rewrite `DockStoreStreamTests.swift` stale tests so stale host freshness is not `.partial`.
203	- Update `AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift` so stale is not online-like.
204	- Rewrite `DockRenderProjectorTests.swift` cached pinned tests to assert a degraded placeholder, not fabricated card data.
205	- Add a "client does not recompute card recency" test.
206	
207	Gates:
208	
209	```bash
210	rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
211	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
212	rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
213	```
214	
215	### Phase 4: Delete Side Doors And Their Tests
216	
217	This is where drift becomes hard to reintroduce.
218	
219	Changes:
220	
221	- Delete shipped `relay/state/snapshot` route and its snapshot-oracle tests.
222	- Delete shipped `state/query` route and `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs` coverage for it.
223	- Remove app-facing downstream route cases for `thread/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, and `thread/loaded/list`.
224	- Keep internal relay helper functions only where canonical projection uses them.
225	- Remove Swift `threadList` tests and real-host smoke tests that treat `thread/list` as app proof.
226	- Update `DiagnosticsLoggingTests.swift`, `SystemHealthProjectorTests.swift`, and `AppServerClientTests.swift` for the removal of app-critical `thread/list` registration.
227	- Rewrite `scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` cases that encode old "no turn warming" behavior.
228	- Replace `ThreadCardFixtureQuery` scope-style tests in `CodexDockTests/DockStoreTestSupport.swift` with direct `DockThreadCardDTO` stream fixtures.
229	
230	Tests:
231	
232	- Removed routes return unsupported method.
233	- Dock freshness proof uses only `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/subscribe`, `archive/update`, and `archive/resync`.
234	- No test proves card correctness by calling `thread/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, `thread/loaded/list`, `relay/state/snapshot`, or `state/query`.
235	
236	Gate:
237	
238	```bash
239	rtk npm run test:relay
240	rtk swift test
241	```
242	
243	### Phase 5: Document Invariants In Code And Docs
244	
245	Add comments where future edits are likely to recreate drift.
246	
247	Required comments:
248	
249	- `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`: canonical fold function comment saying this is the only place raw list/read/turn/live/session-index facts collapse into Dock card facts.
250	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs`: `normalizeThread` comment saying input must already be canonical card facts and must not read raw side-door sources.
251	- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`: reconciliation/storage comment saying stored `threads` rows are the client card source and live lease fields must not be overlaid after storage.
252	- `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`: `activityAtMs` description saying it is canonical latest user-visible activity, not just thread `updatedAt`.
253	- `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`: render-only ordering comment saying relay `orderKey` is semantic order.
254	- `CodexDock/State/LocalThreadMetadataStore.swift`: local metadata comment saying pins/labels/rails are local, but title/status/activity/summary are not.
255	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift`: freshness comment saying transport reachability and Dock data freshness are separate.
256	
257	Docs:
258	
259	- Link this plan from `docs/CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md`.
260	- Update `README.md` so it says relay projection may inspect latest turns, but Swift still consumes only `dock/*` and `archive/*` card streams.
261	- Mark the audit drift inventory as resolved only after the corresponding code and tests land.
262	
263	Final gate:
264	
265	```bash
266	rtk npm run test:relay
267	rtk npm run contract:check
268	rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
269	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
270	rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
271	rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'
272	```
273	
274	## Explicit Non-Goals
275	
276	- Do not make Swift call `thread/turns/list` to repair Dock cards.
277	- Do not keep `state/query` or `relay/state/snapshot` as test-only proof paths.
278	- Do not add a second DTO or v2 card schema to paper over source drift.
279	- Do not preserve cached pinned display as a "safety net."
280	- Do not build a full live turn-event ingestor in this pass.
281	
282	## Known Residual Gap
283	
284	The bounded latest-turn scan fixes live threads and the visible/publish window. A non-live thread outside that window can still have newer turns than `thread/list.updatedAt` and remain mis-ranked until it enters the scan set.
285	
286	That gap is accepted for this pass because the full incremental ingestor is new machinery and would be a larger source of drift risk. If this gap matters after the main fix, the follow-up should still re-use the same canonical projection path instead of adding a second card source.
287	
288

# Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan - 2026-05-31

## Bottom Line

The intended user experience is simple: Dock shows a flat, newest-first list of the work that most recently happened. Manual pins may keep a thread visible, but they must not invent recency, status, title, summary, or activity.

The implementation path is also simple at the architectural level: make the relay card projection the single semantic owner. Swift renders the card stream. It does not repair, reorder, or re-source card truth.

Related audit: [Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit](CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md).

## Model Consensus

This plan was built from the requested parallel model-consensus run:

- Model A: `claude-opus-4-8`, effort `max`.
- Model B: `gpt-5.5`, effort `high`.
- Artifacts: `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-single-source-contract-20260531T183258Z/`.

Consensus result:

- One relay projection folds raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, live status, and session-index identity into one stored card.
- `DockThreadCardDTO` remains the app-facing card shape.
- `activityAtMs`, `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `displaySummary`, card `status`, and freshness are relay-owned card semantics.
- Swift becomes render-only for card truth.
- Card-truth side-door routes and tests are deleted or internalized.
- Ops-health endpoints stay, but they cannot be presented as data freshness.

## Non-Negotiable Invariant

Every Dock and Archive card's recency, ordering, summary, status, and freshness are computed once by the relay projection from a canonical per-thread activity timestamp.

Canonical activity is:

```text
max(thread.updatedAt, thread.createdAt, newest turn timestamp, live event timestamp)
```

The relay persists that activity and derives `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `activityAtMs`, `displaySummary`, `status`, and `freshness` from it. Swift consumes only the `dock/*` and `archive/*` card streams for card list truth.

## Key Root Cause

The current Dock path is shape-safe but source-unsafe:

- Shape-safe: `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` generates `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift`.
- Source-unsafe: `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` and `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` can build cards from `thread/list` and `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while the newest work may exist only in `thread/turns/list`.

That is how the app can show old work at the top while the latest work exists in the raw thread-turn data.

## Canonical Owner

Canonical card truth belongs here:

- Projection/reconcile: `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`.
- Projection semantics: `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs`.
- Raw data folding: `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`.
- Stored card state: `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
- App-facing shape: `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
- Swift decoded shape: `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift`.

The Swift client may format dates and render UI. It may filter/search/group visible rows. It must not compute card recency, card order, card status, card freshness, or card summary from another source.

## Source Disposition

| Source | Current role | Final role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw `thread/list` | Dock/Archive row enumeration and stale timestamp source. | Internal relay input only. Never app-facing card proof. |
| Raw `thread/read` | Detail read and Dock enrichment with `includeTurns:false`. | Detail route stays app-facing. Relay card projection uses it internally for thread metadata. |
| Raw `thread/turns/list` | Thread Detail and oracle/audit paths; Dock does not use it for cards. | Detail route stays app-facing. Relay projection uses bounded latest-turn reads for card recency. |
| Raw `thread/search` | Diagnostic/oracle side door. | Remove app-facing relay route. Keep no card-proof tests on it. |
| Raw `thread/goal/get` | Diagnostic/oracle side door. | Remove app-facing relay route unless a non-card feature later owns it explicitly. |
| Raw `thread/loaded/list` | Live membership/status input. | Internal relay input only. No app-facing card proof. |
| `$CODEX_HOME/session_index.jsonl` | Can supplement rows with candidate metadata. | ID-only discovery input. Display fields come from canonical relay projection. |
| `threads` SQLite table | Stored card rows plus read-time live lease overlay. | Single stored card source. No read-time overlay mutates emitted card truth. |
| `live_leases` | Read-time status overlay. | Internal projection input; live status is folded before storage/emission. |
| `ThreadSummaryCache` | Wired relay-side summary helper/cache. | Absorb into canonical projection; keep only pure latest-safe-turn summary helper if needed. |
| Swift local metadata | Pins, labels, rails, and cached pinned display. | Pins, labels, rails, pin order only. No title/status/activity/summary fallback. |
| `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz` | Ops/transport health. | Keep. They are not card truth and must not be shown as data freshness. |

## Endpoint Disposition

| Endpoint / route | Final decision | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dock/subscribe` | Keep | Primary active card stream. |
| `dock/update` | Keep | Primary active delta stream. |
| `dock/resync` | Keep | Primary active resync path. |
| `archive/subscribe` | Keep | Primary archive card stream. |
| `archive/update` | Keep | Primary archive delta stream. |
| `archive/resync` | Keep | Primary archive resync path. |
| `thread/read` | Keep | Thread Detail legitimately needs raw thread data. Not a Dock card list source. |
| `thread/turns/list` | Keep | Thread Detail legitimately needs turns. Relay projection also uses it internally. |
| `thread/resume` | Keep | Thread Detail live/resume path. |
| `thread/list` | Remove as app-facing route | Raw list is not card truth and is currently a stale side door. |
| `thread/search` | Remove as app-facing route | Search results cannot be a global card source. |
| `thread/goal/get` | Remove as app-facing card route | Goal data is not Dock card truth. |
| `thread/loaded/list` | Remove as app-facing route | Live membership is relay input, not app card truth. |
| `relay/state/snapshot` | Delete shipped route and tests | It is an oracle side door. Tests must prove through app card streams. |
| `state/query` | Delete shipped route and tests | It bypasses stream sequencing and trains tests on the wrong path. |

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 0: Add Canonical Relay Recency

Add canonical recency without changing Swift yet.

Changes:

- Add one canonical card-row read/fold path in `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`, for example `readCanonicalDockThreadRows(...)`.
- In `reconcileDock`, after draining `thread/list`, fetch newest turn data only for:
  - live-leased threads
  - top-N visible/publish-window candidates
- Use `thread/turns/list` with `sortDirection: "desc"` and page size/concurrency constants in `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs`.
- Reuse existing turns-desc patterns from `scripts/dock-relay-state-snapshot.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`, and `scripts/dock-relay-probe.mjs`.
- Set canonical activity as `max(updatedAt, createdAt, newestTurn, liveEvent)`.
- Generalize the activity-derived Archive order key and use it for active Dock too.
- Stop using active Dock list ordinal `dockOrderKey(index, ...)` as semantic ordering.
- Add a stored canonical activity column in `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
- Fix `mergeAuthoritativeThreadRead(...)` so merging `thread/read includeTurns:false` cannot delete or downgrade newer turn activity.

Tests:

- New relay regression: stale `thread/read.updatedAt`, newer `thread/turns/list.startedAt`, card uses the newer turn for `activityAtMs`, `activityAt`, and `orderKey`.
- New relay ordering test: `listDockCards` order equals canonical activity order.
- Rewrite the old "activity from thread fields" assertions, including the old `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs` cases that assume no turn warming.

Gate:

```bash
rtk npm run test:relay
rtk npm run contract:check
```

### Phase 1: Make Live Status Part Of Projection, Not A Read-Time Overlay

The stored card row should already contain the live status that the client sees.

Changes:

- Remove read-time `applyLeaseToCard` mutation from `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
- Fold live status into canonical projection before `upsertThreadCard`.
- Lease acquisition, status change, and expiry must schedule recompute and delta publish.
- Keep lease status status-only: it must not mutate activity, order, summary, title, or freshness.
- Collapse `LiveStatusCache` plus `live_leases` into one source feeding `SessionRouter` and card projection.
- Absorb `ThreadSummaryCache` into the canonical projection. It is wired today, so do not delete it as "unused"; remove its construction site only when the canonical projection owns the equivalent behavior.
- Make session-index supplements ID-only.
- Change supplement validation so one bad supplemental candidate fails that candidate, not the entire host freshness.

Tests:

- Expired lease falls back to projected status and never leaves stale `running`.
- Lease status changes do not change activity, order, summary, or title.
- Live-only thread appears through canonical projection, not through a lease overlay.
- Session-index candidate can contribute an ID, but stale session-index `updatedAt` cannot win.
- Supplemental validation failure marks that candidate failed without poisoning all host freshness.

Gate:

```bash
rtk npm run test:relay
```

### Phase 2: Tighten The Contract

After the relay always emits canonical activity, make the schema enforce that clients receive it.

Changes:

- Make `activityAtMs` required in `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.
- Regenerate `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` using the repo's contract generation path.
- Add fixtures under `contract/dock/fixtures/` for:
  - stale thread-level timestamp but newer turn timestamp
  - stale retained host freshness
  - live status projection
- Replace keyword-style confidence in `scripts/check-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs` with real JSON-Schema fixture validation.

Gate:

```bash
rtk npm run contract:check
```

### Phase 3: Make Swift Render-Only For Card Truth

Swift still owns presentation, but not semantic card truth.

Changes:

- In `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`, remove the `lastActivityDate`-first ordering workaround once relay `orderKey` is canonical.
- Sort card rows by relay `orderKey` for body rows and groups.
- Keep local search, filters, grouping, facets, counts, and relative-time formatting.
- In `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardRowProjector.swift`, consume required `activityAtMs` as the display date source; remove ISO fallback and `.distantPast` card-truth behavior.
- Delete `LocalPinnedDisplaySnapshot` / `lastKnownPinnedDisplay` as a card-data source.
- Render pinned-but-missing rows as explicitly not loaded while preserving label, rail, and pin order.
- Add first-class stale state in `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)`, `AppConnectivityStore`, and global status UI.
- `.stale` must not be online-like.
- Remove `thread/list` from app-critical health in `CodexDock/Diagnostics/ObservabilityContract.swift` and `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift`.
- Remove `AppServerClient.threadList` if no legitimate non-card production caller remains.
- Prefer one stream reducer: move Archive and cleanup away from loose collector behavior if it duplicates `ThreadCardTable`.

Tests:

- Rewrite `DockStoreTestsProjection.swift` ordering tests to assert Swift preserves relay `orderKey`.
- Rewrite `DockStoreStreamTests.swift` stale tests so stale host freshness is not `.partial`.
- Update `AppConnectivityStoreTests.swift` so stale is not online-like.
- Rewrite `DockRenderProjectorTests.swift` cached pinned tests to assert a degraded placeholder, not fabricated card data.
- Add a "client does not recompute card recency" test.

Gates:

```bash
rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
```

### Phase 4: Delete Side Doors And Their Tests

This is where drift becomes hard to reintroduce.

Changes:

- Delete shipped `relay/state/snapshot` route and its snapshot-oracle tests.
- Delete shipped `state/query` route and `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs` coverage for it.
- Remove app-facing downstream route cases for `thread/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, and `thread/loaded/list`.
- Keep internal relay helper functions only where canonical projection uses them.
- Remove Swift `threadList` tests and real-host smoke tests that treat `thread/list` as app proof.
- Update `DiagnosticsLoggingTests.swift`, `SystemHealthProjectorTests.swift`, and `AppServerClientTests.swift` for the removal of app-critical `thread/list` registration.
- Rewrite `scripts/dock-relay-phase5.test.mjs` cases that encode old "no turn warming" behavior.
- Replace `ThreadCardFixtureQuery` scope-style tests in `CodexDockTests/DockStoreTestSupport.swift` with direct `DockThreadCardDTO` stream fixtures.

Tests:

- Removed routes return unsupported method.
- Dock freshness proof uses only `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/subscribe`, `archive/update`, and `archive/resync`.
- No test proves card correctness by calling `thread/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, `thread/loaded/list`, `relay/state/snapshot`, or `state/query`.

Gate:

```bash
rtk npm run test:relay
rtk swift test
```

### Phase 5: Document Invariants In Code And Docs

Add comments where future edits are likely to recreate drift.

Required comments:

- `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`: canonical fold function comment saying this is the only place raw list/read/turn/live/session-index facts collapse into Dock card facts.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs`: `normalizeThread` comment saying input must already be canonical card facts and must not read raw side-door sources.
- `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`: reconciliation/storage comment saying stored `threads` rows are the client card source and live lease fields must not be overlaid after storage.
- `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`: `activityAtMs` description saying it is canonical latest user-visible activity, not just thread `updatedAt`.
- `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`: render-only ordering comment saying relay `orderKey` is semantic order.
- `CodexDock/State/LocalThreadMetadataStore.swift`: local metadata comment saying pins/labels/rails are local, but title/status/activity/summary are not.
- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift`: freshness comment saying transport reachability and Dock data freshness are separate.

Docs:

- Link this plan from `docs/CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md`.
- Update `README.md` so it says relay projection may inspect latest turns, but Swift still consumes only `dock/*` and `archive/*` card streams.
- Mark the audit drift inventory as resolved only after the corresponding code and tests land.

Final gate:

```bash
rtk npm run test:relay
rtk npm run contract:check
rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'
```

## Explicit Non-Goals

- Do not make Swift call `thread/turns/list` to repair Dock cards.
- Do not keep `state/query` or `relay/state/snapshot` as test-only proof paths.
- Do not add a second DTO or v2 card schema to paper over source drift.
- Do not preserve cached pinned display as a "safety net."
- Do not build a full live turn-event ingestor in this pass.

## Known Residual Gap

The bounded latest-turn scan fixes live threads and the visible/publish window. A non-live thread outside that window can still have newer turns than `thread/list.updatedAt` and remain mis-ranked until it enters the scan set.

That gap is accepted for this pass because the full incremental ingestor is new machinery and would be a larger source of drift risk. If this gap matters after the main fix, the follow-up should still re-use the same canonical projection path instead of adding a second card source.

3	## Bottom Line
4	
5	The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.
6	
7	The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.
8	
9	Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).
10	
11	## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug
12	
13	Observed on 2026-05-31:
14	
15	- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
16	- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
17	- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
18	  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
19	  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
20	- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.
21	
22	Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.

332	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
333	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
334	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
335	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
336	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
337	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
338	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
339	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
340	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |

342	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
343	
344	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
345	
346	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
347	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
348	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
349	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
350	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
351	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
352	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
353	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
354	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
355	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
356	
357	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
358	
359	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
360	
361	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
362	
363	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
364	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
365	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
366	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
367	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
368	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
369	
370	## Verdict
371	
372	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
373	
374	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31

## Bottom Line

The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.

The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.

Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).

## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug

Observed on 2026-05-31:

- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.

Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.

## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects

The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.

Line audit:

| File | Lines | What it protects | What it does not protect |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 6-23 | Every stream update must have `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `view`, `epoch`, and `seq`; schema version is fixed at `2`. | It does not say where `activityAtMs` must come from. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 30-95 | The stream may carry `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, `freshness`, hosts, cards, upserts, and deletes. | It does not prove a complete stream inspected turns. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 97-124 | Old session/message fields are explicitly rejected. | It only rejects obsolete fields; it does not validate semantic freshness. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 157-191 | Host-level freshness has `unknown`, `fresh`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`. | It does not define row-level freshness behavior during retained stale rows. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 223-240 | Card required fields include `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `displaySummary`, `title`, `status`, `sourceKind`, `lane`, `archiveState`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | It requires these fields to exist, not to be derived from the latest real work. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 269-282 | `orderKey`, `activityAt`, and optional `activityAtMs` exist in the payload. | It does not say whether order uses list ordinal, thread `updatedAt`, latest turn time, or lease time. |
| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 1-2 | Swift DTO is generated from that schema. | Generated Swift mirrors shape only. |
| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 342-365 | Swift decodes the card fields exactly as the relay sends them. | Swift has no second source for newer card activity. |

## Exhaustive Contract Surface Map

This section is the missing contract map. It separates three things that had
been blurred together:

1. The source that owns data.
2. The endpoint that exposes or transforms that data.
3. The app or script that consumes that endpoint.

The important point: the generated `DockThreadCard` contract covers only the
card stream shape. It does not cover every source, every relay route, or every
consumer that can affect what the user sees.

### Undocumented Contract Gaps

These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:

1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.

| `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` | 267-281 | Reconcile enriches list rows as human-started rows and session-index supplements. | Still thread rows only. |

| `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` | 640-643 | Human-started enrichment defaults to `thread/read { includeTurns:false }`. | The validation/enrichment path explicitly excludes turns. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` | 623-637 | `mergeAuthoritativeThreadRead` lets `thread/read` fields override list fields and deletes `turns`. | A stale `thread/read.updatedAt` can replace fresher list data, and turns are removed. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` | 705-710 | Session-index supplements also validate with `thread/read includeTurns:false`. | Supplements can add missing rows but not turn-derived recency. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` | 872-907 | `aggregateThreadList` returns enriched thread rows plus live overlay metadata. | Raw `thread/list` still does not become turn-aware. |

### 4. Card projection chooses thread timestamps

Line audit:

| File | Lines | Behavior | Drift point |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` | 192-205 | Thread preference compares status priority, then `updatedAt ?? createdAt`. | Turn timestamps are ignored when choosing between candidate rows. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 182-185 | `dockOrderKey` is based on list ordinal plus thread id. | Active Dock order is not activity-time-derived. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 269-279 | `overlayLiveStatus` copies live `status` and `sessionId` only. | It does not copy activity time, summary, title, repo, or branch. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 281-310 | `orderedDockRows` overlays live rows onto existing rows but does not add live-only rows. | A live thread absent from list/supplements can stay absent from Dock cards. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 312-349 | `normalizeThread` sets `activityAtMs` from `thread.activityAt` else `rowTimestamp(thread)`. | `rowTimestamp` is still `updatedAt ?? createdAt`; no `thread/turns/list`. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 333-344 | The final card carries `activityAt`, `activityAtMs`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | These fields look canonical to Swift even when derived from stale thread metadata. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 352-381 | Stored cards are reconstructed from SQLite. | Cached stale activity can keep flowing forward. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-views.mjs` | 384-399 | Lease overlay on stored cards changes `backendSessionID` and status only. | Leases do not repair stale activity/order/summary. |

### 5. SQLite persists the projected card, not the raw truth

Line audit:

| File | Lines | Behavior | Drift point |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 130-154 | `threads` stores `order_key`, `activity_at`, `activity_at_ms`, `display_summary`, `status`, `updated_at_ms`, `freshness_status`, and `raw_json`. | Persisted state stores projected card values. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 159-167 | `thread_field_provenance` exists as a table. | It is not used by Dock card ordering or recency. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 169-179 | `sync_scopes` stores complete/incomplete sync status. | Freshness is scope-level, not proof of latest turn activity. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 182-190 | `live_leases` stores endpoint, backend session, status, waiting state, capability. | No activity fields exist in the lease table. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 394-430 | `listDockCards` orders by `t.order_key ASC`, then applies lease status. | Store read order follows projected list ordinal, not latest real activity. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 570-599 | `applyDockReconciliation` compares projected cards and publishes upserts. | It publishes projected changes only. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 601-608 | Missing rows are deleted only when reconciliation is complete. | Incomplete refresh intentionally keeps stale rows visible. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 703-779 | `upsertThreadCard` writes `updated_at_ms = card.activityAtMs` and `freshness_status = card.freshness || "fresh"`. | The DB has no independent raw `thread.updatedAt` or latest-turn timestamp. |

Line audit:

| File | Lines | Behavior | Drift point |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs` | 369-392 | `freshnessForHost` returns `stale` if any sync scope for that host has `complete = 0`. | One failed scope can make the host stale; no row-level proof. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` | 308-323 | Reconcile publishes `freshness` from `freshnessForHost`. | A card can remain stale while the host says fresh, or vice versa. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` | 483-549 | Dock snapshots include store cards plus host freshness. | Snapshot `complete` means window coverage, not turn inspection. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` | 552-572 | Archive snapshots use the same host freshness source. | Archive failures can affect host-level health language even when Dock rows are present. |

### 7. Live leases are a separate clock

Line audit:

| File | Lines | Behavior | Drift point |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` | 51-59 | `LiveStatusCache` collects live rows with `includeHistory:false`. | Detail routing and Dock lease refresh do not share the exact same source set. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs` | 441-468 | `refreshLiveLeases` collects live rows with `includeHistory:true` and writes `live_leases`. | The lease table can differ from detail routing cache. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs` | 12-46 | Live overlay can be `ready`, `degraded`, `stale`, `unavailable`, or `disabled`. | This overlay is separate from Dock stream freshness. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs` | 94-143 | Cache refresh records live rows and failures on its own timer. | It is not automatically synchronized with every Dock reconcile. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs` | 178-186 | Detail route selection uses cache row lookup and falls back to history. | Detail can route history while Dock lease still says live, or the reverse. |

Net: leases were never unified with the card contract. They are an overlay with their own expiry, not the source of card activity truth.

## Swift Client Touchpoints

Line audit:

| File | Lines | Behavior | Drift point |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 342-365 | Swift card DTO contains `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `activityAtMs`, title, summary, status, freshness, completeness. | Swift trusts relay values. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 82-112 | Snapshot application replaces cards with stream cards after schema/window validation. | Validation checks shape and stream continuity, not semantic recency. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 115-168 | Delta application upserts/deletes cards and enforces sequence/epoch rules. | Again, no turn-derived repair. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift` | 321-350 | Host status maps stale/offline/error with retained rows to `.partial`. | User can see rows while data is stale by design. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardRowProjector.swift` | 27-58 | `DockThreadCardDTO` becomes `DockRowViewModel`. | Row model gets whatever activity the relay sent. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardRowProjector.swift` | 118-130 | Row activity uses `activityAtMs` first, then parses `activityAt`. | No fallback to `thread/turns/list` exists on the overview. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardRowProjector.swift` | 15-24 and 61-89 | Pinned cached rows can be rendered from local metadata. | A pinned row can remain visible without current relay card data. |
| `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` | 563-574 | Thread detail explicitly calls `thread/read includeTurns:false`, then drains all turns. | Detail can be current while Dock overview stays stale. |

## Connectivity And Route Health Touchpoints

Line audit:

| File | Lines | Behavior | Drift point |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 848-855 | `/readyz` returns process-level OK. | It does not check raw app-server or Dock freshness. |
| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 763-767 | `/statusz` runs raw app-server health then returns status snapshot. | Top-level status response can be OK while routes/state have failures. |
| `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` | 783-794 | `/routesz` returns route health evidence. | Route health is not the same as data freshness. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs` | 205-260 | Status snapshot includes `appCriticalFailures`, route list, live status, state, and errors. | Callers must inspect nested fields; `ok:true` alone is not enough. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 291-355 | Route operations start as partial. | A running request can look partial independent of Dock data quality. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 358-375 | Route operations finish from request success/failure. | A successful stale payload can still mark route success. |
| `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs` | 514-516 | `appCriticalFailures` only includes routes with `routeStatus == failed`. | Stale/incomplete data may not become an app-critical failure. |

## Drift Inventory

| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |

## Tests That Encode Current Behavior

These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:

- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.

## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard

This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.

The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:

1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.

## Verdict

The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.

The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

1	# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31
2	
3	## Bottom Line
4	
5	The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.
6	
7	The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.

181

330	| --- | --- | --- |
331	| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
332	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
333	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
334	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
335	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
336	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
337	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
338	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
339	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
340	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |
341	
342	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
343	
344	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
345	
346	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
347	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
348	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
349	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
350	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
351	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
352	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
353	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
354	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
355	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
356	
357	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
358	
359	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
360	
361	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
362	
363	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
364	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
365	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
366	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
367	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
368	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
369	
370	## Verdict
371	
372	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
373	
374	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31

## Bottom Line

The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.

The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.

Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).

## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug

Observed on 2026-05-31:

- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.

Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.

## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects

The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.

Line audit:

| File | Lines | What it protects | What it does not protect |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 6-23 | Every stream update must have `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `view`, `epoch`, and `seq`; schema version is fixed at `2`. | It does not say where `activityAtMs` must come from. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 30-95 | The stream may carry `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, `freshness`, hosts, cards, upserts, and deletes. | It does not prove a complete stream inspected turns. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 97-124 | Old session/message fields are explicitly rejected. | It only rejects obsolete fields; it does not validate semantic freshness. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 157-191 | Host-level freshness has `unknown`, `fresh`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`. | It does not define row-level freshness behavior during retained stale rows. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 223-240 | Card required fields include `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `displaySummary`, `title`, `status`, `sourceKind`, `lane`, `archiveState`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | It requires these fields to exist, not to be derived from the latest real work. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 269-282 | `orderKey`, `activityAt`, and optional `activityAtMs` exist in the payload. | It does not say whether order uses list ordinal, thread `updatedAt`, latest turn time, or lease time. |
| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 1-2 | Swift DTO is generated from that schema. | Generated Swift mirrors shape only. |
| `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | 342-365 | Swift decodes the card fields exactly as the relay sends them. | Swift has no second source for newer card activity. |
| `scripts/generate-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs` | 500-518 | `npm run contract:check` fails if generated Swift is stale. | The generator cannot detect bad source selection inside relay projection. |

Net: we made payload-shape drift hard. We did not make data-source drift hard.

## Exhaustive Contract Surface Map

This section is the missing contract map. It separates three things that had
been blurred together:

1. The source that owns data.
2. The endpoint that exposes or transforms that data.
3. The app or script that consumes that endpoint.

The important point: the generated `DockThreadCard` contract covers only the
card stream shape. It does not cover every source, every relay route, or every
consumer that can affect what the user sees.

### Data Planes

| Plane | What it is | Primary owners | Primary consumers | Contract status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raw Codex history | The app-server at `historyUrl`; relay reads it through pooled JSON-RPC. | `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:38-48`, `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:552-566` | Relay `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, Dock reconcile | Not covered by `DockThreadCard`; raw `ThreadDTO`/list/detail shapes. |
| Live upstream sessions | Current app-server sessions found through `thread/loaded/list` and `thread/read`. | `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs:92-120`, `scripts/dock-relay-live-status-cache.mjs:94-153` | `SessionRouter`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live leases | Not covered except when projected into a card stream. |
| Relay SQLite projection | `.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`; stores projected cards, sync scopes, changes, and live leases. | `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:124-195`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs:535-620` | `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/*`, diagnostics | Card rows are covered after projection; DB-only fields are not. |
| Generated card contract | JSON schema plus generated Swift DTO for card stream updates. | `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`, `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` | Dock, Archive, cleanup, snapshot loader | Covers shape, enum vocabulary, stream version, and required fields. Does not cover freshness source. |
| Swift local metadata | User-owned local pin/label/rail display state. | `CodexDock/State/LocalThreadMetadataStore.swift:3-120`, `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift:83-105` | Dock projection, Archive, Archive cleanup | Not covered; it is a local overlay keyed by card identity. |
| Detail/live event stream | Raw thread turns, notifications, and server requests after opening a thread. | `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:563-625`, `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:446-524` | Thread Detail, composer, request cards | Not covered by `DockThreadCard`; mostly `ThreadDTO`, turn DTOs, and raw `JSONValue`. |
| Observability | Route health, traces, metrics, status snapshots. | `scripts/dock-relay-observability.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs` | Connectivity UI, diagnostics, Makefile targets, audits | Not a data contract for rows. |

### Undocumented Contract Gaps

These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:

1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.
