327	## Drift Inventory
328	
329	| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
330	| --- | --- | --- |
331	| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
332	| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
333	| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
334	| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
335	| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
336	| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
337	| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
338	| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
339	| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
340	| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |
341	
342	## Tests That Encode Current Behavior
343	
344	These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:
345	
346	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
347	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
348	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
349	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
350	- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
351	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
352	- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
353	- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
354	- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
355	- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.
356	
357	## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard
358	
359	This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.
360	
361	The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:
362	
363	1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
364	2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
365	3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
366	4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
367	5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
368	6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.
369	
370	## Verdict
371	
372	The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.
373	
374	The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31

## Bottom Line

The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.

The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.

Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).

## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug

Observed on 2026-05-31:

- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.

Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.

## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects

The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.

Line audit:

| --- | ---: | --- | --- |

| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 30-95 | The stream may carry `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, `freshness`, hosts, cards, upserts, and deletes. | It does not prove a complete stream inspected turns. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 97-124 | Old session/message fields are explicitly rejected. | It only rejects obsolete fields; it does not validate semantic freshness. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 157-191 | Host-level freshness has `unknown`, `fresh`, `stale`, `offline`, `error`. | It does not define row-level freshness behavior during retained stale rows. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 223-240 | Card required fields include `orderKey`, `activityAt`, `displaySummary`, `title`, `status`, `sourceKind`, `lane`, `archiveState`, `freshness`, and `completeness`. | It requires these fields to exist, not to be derived from the latest real work. |
| `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` | 269-282 | `orderKey`, `activityAt`, and optional `activityAtMs` exist in the payload. | It does not say whether order uses list ordinal, thread `updatedAt`, latest turn time, or lease time. |

### Undocumented Contract Gaps

These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:

1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.

## Drift Inventory

| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |

## Tests That Encode Current Behavior

These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:

- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.

## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard

This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.

The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:

1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.

## Verdict

The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.

The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

# Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit - 2026-05-31

## Bottom Line

The drift is real. The generated Dock card contract keeps the JSON payload shape aligned between relay and Swift, but it does not unify the semantic source of truth for activity time, row order, live lease state, host freshness, or turn-level updates.

The exact failure mode is: Dock cards are built from thread-level `thread/list` plus `thread/read includeTurns:false`, while current work can live only in `thread/turns/list` or live turn events. Nothing currently promotes those newer turn timestamps into Dock `activityAtMs`, `orderKey`, summary, row freshness, or persisted relay state.

Implementation plan: [Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan](CODEX_DOCK_DATA_CONTRACT_SINGLE_SOURCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-05-31.md).

## Runtime Evidence From The Current Bug

Observed on 2026-05-31:

- Active thread: `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1`.
- `thread/read` returned `updatedAt=1780238608`, which is `2026-05-31T14:43:28Z`.
- `thread/turns/list` returned newer turns:
  - `startedAt=1780249079`, `2026-05-31T17:37:59Z`, status `interrupted`.
  - `startedAt=1780246962`, `2026-05-31T17:02:42Z`, status `completed`.
- `dock/subscribe` used the stale thread-level activity timestamp, so the card sorted as old even though current turn activity existed.

Plain English: the relay did not lose the current work. It was visible on the turn-detail route. The Dock overview simply never looked at that route when creating the card.

## What The Existing Generated Contract Actually Protects

The canonical card payload shape is `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`.

### Undocumented Contract Gaps

These are the places where the current data contract lets the system drift:

1. `activityAt` has no canonical source. It might come from `thread.activityAt`, `thread.updatedAt`, `thread.createdAt`, list ordinal, or a cached row. The schema only requires the field to exist.
2. `orderKey` has no semantic rule. Active Dock uses list ordinal order; Archive uses activity-derived order; the client may sort again by local activity date.
3. `displaySummary` has no freshness rule. It can be derived from thread-level metadata even when newer turn content exists.
4. `thread/turns/list` is the detail source for newest work, but the card stream contract does not require Dock cards to inspect it.
5. Live leases are status overlays only. They do not carry or repair `activityAt`, `orderKey`, `title`, `displaySummary`, repo, branch, or working directory.
6. `LiveStatusCache` and SQLite `live_leases` have separate lifecycles. Detail routing can disagree with Dock lease overlay.
7. Host freshness is scope-level. A host can be stale while rows remain visible, and a row can look fresh while its semantic source is stale.
8. Local pin metadata is a separate display cache. It can keep a pinned row visible with old title/status/activity when no current card exists.
9. `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`, `/statez`, `/syncz`, `/explainz`, and parity scripts are useful truth/oracle surfaces, but they are not the app card contract.
10. Route health is not row freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and traces can be green while card ordering is wrong.
11. Thread Detail has its own raw event/request contract. Request cards and turn events can drift independently from `DockThreadCard`.
12. Contract checks protect only a small fixture set and generated Swift text. They do not run full JSON Schema validation against broad runtime examples.

## Drift Inventory

| Drift point | Root cause | User-visible result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current turn activity not on top | Dock never reads `thread/turns/list` during card reconcile. | A thread with active recent work appears old. |
| Old card summary/title | Summary comes from thread row fields, not latest turn content. | Card text can lag behind current conversation. |
| `orderKey` vs activity | Active Dock `orderKey` is list ordinal. | Store ordering can preserve stale list order. |
| `activityAtMs` vs turn timestamps | `activityAtMs` is projected from `activityAt` or thread `updatedAt/createdAt`. | Client cannot sort by real newest work if relay timestamp is stale. |
| Lease status vs card data | Leases update status/session only. | A live-looking card can still have old title/activity. |
| Expired lease edge | Expired lease only downgrades dormant cards. | A stored `running` status can survive lease expiry. |
| Live detail route vs Dock lease route | `LiveStatusCache` and `refreshLiveLeases` use different timing/source sets. | Detail and Dock can disagree about what is live. |
| Host freshness vs row freshness | `freshnessForHost` is scope-based; rows are retained. | UI can show data while also saying partial/stale. |
| Route health vs data freshness | Route observability measures request outcome, not payload semantic age. | `/readyz` or route health can look OK while Dock data is stale. |
| Generated schema confidence | Schema validates shape, not source semantics. | `contract:check` can pass while user-facing ordering is wrong. |

## Tests That Encode Current Behavior

These tests are useful guardrails, but several of them encode the behavior that makes the current bug possible:

- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:206` - stale scope keeps existing rows visible.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:243` - live lease publishes status-only card changes.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:292` - expired lease behavior is tested for the dormant case.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:628` - fresh cached `dock/subscribe` can skip refresh.
- `scripts/dock-relay.test.mjs:1280` - Dock card activity comes from thread fields.
- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:190` - `/readyz` can pass while Dock state freshness is stale.
- `scripts/dock-relay-observability.test.mjs:238` - `dock/subscribe` route health can be healthy while serving stale cached state.
- `CodexDockTests/DockStoreStreamTests.swift:219` - stale heartbeat retains rows as partial.
- `CodexDockTests/ThreadDetailStoreTests.swift:5` and related tests - detail store relies on `thread/turns/list`, which is separate from Dock cards.
- `CodexDockTests/DockRenderProjectorTests.swift:44` - cached pinned rows can render without live cards.

## What Would Make Drift Actually Hard

This is not an implementation plan, just the architectural conclusion from the audit.

The contract would need to define a canonical activity source, not just fields:

1. Dock card recency must mean "latest user-visible thread activity", with a precise priority order such as latest turn timestamp, then live event timestamp, then thread `updatedAt`, then `createdAt`.
2. Relay state must persist that canonical activity timestamp separately from list ordinal and raw `updatedAt`.
3. `orderKey` must be derived from canonical activity, or the client must ignore relay order for global recency.
4. Live leases must either remain a status-only overlay by contract, or explicitly carry activity/summary fields and a freshness source.
5. Route health must not be presented as data freshness. `/readyz` remains process proof only.
6. The generated schema should be extended only if the semantic source can be enforced or tested; otherwise it will keep giving false confidence.

## Verdict

The relay/client contract is not "impossible to drift." It is shape-safe but source-unsafe.

The current user-facing bug is not primarily a Swift display bug. Swift is faithfully displaying stale card fields. The deeper bug is in the relay Dock projection: it treats thread-level rows as canonical for overview recency while the real current work can exist only in turn-level data.

102	        case .responseDecoding(let message):
103	            "Could not decode app-server response: \(message)"
104	        case .server(let error):
105	            "App-server rejected request: \(error.message)"
106	        case .transport(let message):
107	            "App-server transport failed: \(message)"
108	        case .unexpectedServerRequest(let method):
109	            "Unsupported app-server request from server: \(method)"
110	        case .unmatchedResponse(let id):
111	            "App-server sent response for unknown request id `\(id)`"
112	        }

521	    private func sendRequest(
522	        id: JSONRPCRequestID,
523	        method: String,
524	        params: JSONValue?,
525	        timeout: Duration,
526	        allowsConnecting: Bool,
527	        observabilityContext: AppServerRequestObservabilityContext?
528	    ) async throws -> JSONValue {
529	        try ensureCanSend(allowsConnecting: allowsConnecting)
530	
531	        guard pendingRequests[id] == nil else {
532	            DockLog.appServer.error("app-server request duplicate method=\(method, privacy: .public) request_id=\(DockLog.publicID(id), privacy: .public)")
533	            throw AppServerClientError.duplicateRequestID(id)
534	        }
535	
536	        if let observabilityContext {
537	            await observabilityContext.store?.start(observabilityContext)
538	        }
539	        let request = JSONRPCRequest(
540	            id: id,
541	            method: method,
542	            params: paramsWithTraceMetadata(params, context: observabilityContext)
543	        )
544	        let text = try JSONRPCMessage.request(request).jsonString()
545	        DockLog.appServer.info("app-server request started method=\(method, privacy: .public) request_id=\(DockLog.publicID(id), privacy: .public)")
546	
547	        return try await withTaskCancellationHandler {
548	            try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
549	                let timeoutTask = Task { [weak self] in
550	                    do {
551	                        try await Task.sleep(for: timeout)
552	                        await self?.finishPending(
553	                            id: id,
554	                            result: .failure(AppServerClientError.requestTimedOut(id))
555	                        )
556	                    } catch {
557	                        return
558	                    }
559	                }
560	
561	                pendingRequests[id] = PendingRequest(
562	                    method: method,
563	                    startedAt: Date(),
564	                    observabilityContext: observabilityContext,
565	                    continuation: continuation,
566	                    timeoutTask: timeoutTask
567	                )
568	
569	                Task { [weak self] in
570	                    do {
571	                        try await self?.sendRaw(text)
572	                    } catch {
573	                        await self?.finishPending(
574	                            id: id,
575	                            result: .failure(AppServerClientError.transport(error.localizedDescription))
576	                        )
577	                        await self?.handleConnectedSendFailure(error.localizedDescription)
578	                    }
579	                }
580	            }
581	        } onCancel: {
582	            Task { [weak self] in
583	                await self?.finishPending(
584	                    id: id,
585	                    result: .failure(AppServerClientError.requestCancelled(id))
586	                )
587	            }
588	        }
589	    }

597	    private func paramsWithTraceMetadata(
598	        _ params: JSONValue?,
599	        context: AppServerRequestObservabilityContext?
600	    ) -> JSONValue? {
601	        guard let context else {
602	            return params
603	        }
604	        switch params {
605	        case .object(let object):
606	            var next = object
607	            next[ObservabilityContract.traceParamKey] = context.traceJSONValue
608	            return .object(next)
609	        case nil:
610	            return .object([ObservabilityContract.traceParamKey: context.traceJSONValue])
611	        case .array, .bool, .double, .integer, .null, .string:
612	            return params
613	        }
614	    }

629	    private func startReceiveLoop() {
630	        receiveTask?.cancel()
631	        receiveTask = Task { [weak self, transport] in
632	            await self?.logReceiveLoopStarted()
633	            while !Task.isCancelled {
634	                do {
635	                    guard let text = try await transport.receive() else {
636	                        await self?.handleTransportLoss("transport closed")
637	                        return
638	                    }
639	
640	                    let message: JSONRPCMessage
641	                    do {
642	                        message = try JSONRPCMessage.decode(from: text)
643	                    } catch {
644	                        DockLog.appServer.error("app-server received malformed message error=\(DockLog.errorSummary(error), privacy: .public)")
645	                        await self?.failConnection(.malformedMessage(error.localizedDescription))
646	                        return
647	                    }
648	
649	                    await self?.handleIncoming(message)
650	                } catch is CancellationError {
651	                    await self?.logReceiveLoopEnded(reason: "cancelled")
652	                    return
653	                } catch {
654	                    await self?.handleTransportLoss(error.localizedDescription)
655	                    return
656	                }
657	            }
658	        }
659	    }

661	    private func handleTransportLoss(_ reason: String) async {
662	        DockLog.appServer.warning("app-server transport lost reason=\(DockLog.redacted(reason), privacy: .public) reconnect_enabled=\((self.connectionPolicy.reconnect != nil), privacy: .public)")
663	        receiveTask = nil
664	        failAllPending(with: .disconnected(reason))
665	        await transport.disconnect()
666	
667	        guard connectionPolicy.reconnect != nil,
668	              initializeParams != nil,
669	              !isExplicitlyDisconnected else {
670	            markOffline(reason)
671	            return
672	        }
673	
674	        startReconnect(reason: reason)
675	    }
676	
677	    private func startReconnect(reason: String) {
678	        guard reconnectTask == nil else {
679	            return
680	        }
681	        DockLog.appServer.warning("app-server reconnect loop scheduled reason=\(DockLog.redacted(reason), privacy: .public)")
682	        reconnectTask?.cancel()
683	        reconnectTask = Task { [weak self] in
684	            await self?.runReconnectLoop(reason: reason)
685	        }
686	    }
687	
688	    private func runReconnectLoop(reason: String) async {
689	        guard let reconnect = connectionPolicy.reconnect,
690	              let params = initializeParams else {
691	            markOffline(reason)
692	            return
693	        }
694	
695	        var lastErrorReason = reason
696	        for attempt in 1...reconnect.maxAttempts {
697	            guard !Task.isCancelled, !isExplicitlyDisconnected else {
698	                return
699	            }
700	            guard await waitForForegroundWorkIfNeeded() else {
701	                return
702	            }
703	
704	            setState(.reconnecting(attempt: attempt, reason: lastErrorReason))
705	            DockLog.appServer.notice("app-server reconnect attempt started attempt=\(attempt, privacy: .public) max_attempts=\(reconnect.maxAttempts, privacy: .public)")
706	
707	            do {
708	                try await Task.sleep(for: reconnect.delay(for: attempt))
709	            } catch {
710	                return
711	            }
712	
713	            guard !Task.isCancelled, !isExplicitlyDisconnected else {
714	                return
715	            }
716	            guard await waitForForegroundWorkIfNeeded() else {
717	                return
718	            }
719	
720	            do {
721	                try await openTransport(mode: .reconnecting)
722	                _ = try await completeInitializeHandshake(params: params, timeout: initializeTimeout)
723	                reconnectTask = nil
724	                DockLog.appServer.notice("app-server reconnect attempt succeeded attempt=\(attempt, privacy: .public)")
725	                return
726	            } catch {
727	                lastErrorReason = errorFrom(error).localizedDescription
728	                DockLog.appServer.warning("app-server reconnect attempt failed attempt=\(attempt, privacy: .public) error=\(DockLog.redacted(lastErrorReason), privacy: .public)")
729	                failAllPending(with: .disconnected(lastErrorReason))
730	                await transport.disconnect()
731	            }
732	        }
733	
734	        reconnectTask = nil
735	        DockLog.appServer.error("app-server reconnect exhausted attempts=\(reconnect.maxAttempts, privacy: .public) last_error=\(DockLog.redacted(lastErrorReason), privacy: .public)")
736	        markOffline("Reconnect failed after \(reconnect.maxAttempts) attempts: \(lastErrorReason)")
737	    }
738	
739	    private func waitForForegroundWorkIfNeeded() async -> Bool {
740	        guard let foregroundWorkGate else {
741	            return true
742	        }
743	
744	        while !Task.isCancelled, !isExplicitlyDisconnected {
745	            if await foregroundWorkGate.allowsForegroundWork {
746	                return true
747	            }
748	            do {
749	                try await Task.sleep(for: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.foregroundPollInterval)
750	            } catch {
751	                return false

118	    private func activityDate(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> Date {
119	        if let activityAtMs = card.activityAtMs {

121	        }
122	        let fractionalFormatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
123	        fractionalFormatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
124	        if let date = fractionalFormatter.date(from: card.activityAt) {
125	            return date
126	        }
127	        if let date = ISO8601DateFormatter().date(from: card.activityAt) {
128	            return date
129	        }
130	        return .distantPast

140	            return .needsApproval
141	        case .idle:

143	        case .error:

156	        case .agent:
157	            return .agentOrAutomation(subtype: .exec)
158	        case .unknown:
159	            switch card.sourceKind {
160	            case .human:
161	                return .humanInteractive(subtype: .cli)
162	            case .automation:
163	                return .agentOrAutomation(subtype: .exec)
164	            case .unknown:
165	                return .unknown()

170	    private func relativeTime(since date: Date) -> String {
171	        guard date != .distantPast else {
172	            return "No activity"
173	        }
174	        let seconds = max(0, Int(now().timeIntervalSince(date)))
175	
176	        switch seconds {
177	        case 0..<60:
178	            return "now"
179	        case 60..<3_600:
180	            return "\(seconds / 60)m ago"
181	        case 3_600..<86_400:
182	            return "\(seconds / 3_600)h ago"
183	        default:
184	            return "\(seconds / 86_400)d ago"
185	        }
186	    }

202	            (partial &* 31) &+ UInt64(byte)
203	        }
204	        return rails[Int(checksum % UInt64(rails.count))]
205	    }

195	public protocol LocalThreadMetadataStoring: Sendable {
196	    func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
197	    func save(
198	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
199	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
200	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
201	    func save(
202	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
203	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
204	}
205	
206	public actor FileLocalThreadMetadataStore: LocalThreadMetadataStoring {
207	    private struct Entry: Codable {
208	        let key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
209	        let metadata: LocalThreadMetadata
210	    }
211	
212	    private let fileURL: URL
213	    private var cache: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]?
214	
215	    public init(fileURL: URL = FileLocalThreadMetadataStore.defaultFileURL()) {
216	        self.fileURL = fileURL
217	    }
218	
219	    public func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
220	        if let cache {
221	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load cache hit entries=\(cache.count, privacy: .public)")
222	            return cache
223	        }
224	
225	        let loaded: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
226	        if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) {
227	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load started path=\(self.fileURL.path, privacy: .public)")
228	            let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)
229	            let entries = try JSONDecoder().decode([Entry].self, from: data)
230	            loaded = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: entries.map { ($0.key, $0.metadata) })
231	        } else {
232	            loaded = [:]
233	        }
234	        cache = loaded
235	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load finished entries=\(loaded.count, privacy: .public)")
236	        return loaded
237	    }
238	
239	    public func save(
240	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
241	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
242	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
243	        var values = try await load()
244	        if let metadata, !metadata.isEmpty {
245	            values[key] = metadata
246	        } else {
247	            values.removeValue(forKey: key)
248	        }
249	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist started host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(values.count, privacy: .public)")
250	        let persisted = try await save(values)
251	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist finished host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(persisted.count, privacy: .public)")
252	        return persisted
253	    }
254	
255	    public func save(
256	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
257	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
258	        let persistedValues = values.filter { !$0.value.isEmpty }
259	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist started entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
260	        try persist(persistedValues)
261	        cache = persistedValues
262	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist finished entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
263	        return persistedValues
264	    }
265	
266	    private func persist(_ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]) throws {
267	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
268	            at: fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent(),
269	            withIntermediateDirectories: true
270	        )
271	        let entries = values
272	            .map { Entry(key: $0.key, metadata: $0.value) }
273	            .sorted {
274	                [$0.key.hostID, $0.key.backendSessionID, $0.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
275	                    < [$1.key.hostID, $1.key.backendSessionID, $1.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
276	            }
277	        let data = try JSONEncoder().encode(entries)
278	        try data.write(to: fileURL, options: [.atomic])
279	    }
280	
281	    public static func defaultFileURL() -> URL {
282	        let directory = FileManager.default.urls(
283	            for: .applicationSupportDirectory,
284	            in: .userDomainMask
285	        ).first ?? FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
286	        return directory
287	            .appendingPathComponent("CodexDock", isDirectory: true)
288	            .appendingPathComponent("thread-metadata.json")
289	    }
290	}

459	    private func record(
460	        host: DockHostViewModel,
461	        source: ObservationSource,
462	        phase: HostConnectivityPhase,
463	        checked: Bool = true,
464	        checkedAt: Date? = nil,
465	        successAt: Date? = nil
466	    ) {
467	        bootstrapStatus = nil
468	        let timestamp = checkedAt ?? (checked ? now() : nil)
469	        var record = records[host.id] ?? HostRecord(
470	            id: host.id,
471	            displayName: host.displayName,
472	            endpoint: host.endpoint,
473	            observations: [:],
474	            routeDiagnostics: [:],
475	            lifecyclePhase: nil
476	        )
477	        if !hostOrder.contains(host.id) {
478	            hostOrder.append(host.id)
479	        }
480	        let existingObservation = record.observations[source]
481	        let lastSuccessAt: Date?
482	        if let successAt {
483	            lastSuccessAt = successAt
484	        } else if phase.isOnlineLike {
485	            lastSuccessAt = timestamp ?? now()
486	        } else {
487	            lastSuccessAt = existingObservation?.lastSuccessAt
488	        }
489	
490	        record.observations[source] = Observation(
491	            phase: phase,
492	            lastCheckedAt: timestamp ?? existingObservation?.lastCheckedAt,
493	            lastSuccessAt: lastSuccessAt
494	        )
495	        records[host.id] = record
496	        publish()
497	    }

499	    private func publishBootstrapStatusIfNeeded() {

509	    private func publish() {
510	        let nextHosts = records.values
511	            .map(snapshot(from:))
512	            .sorted { lhs, rhs in
513	                let leftIndex = hostIndex(lhs.id)
514	                let rightIndex = hostIndex(rhs.id)
515	                if leftIndex == rightIndex {
516	                    return lhs.displayName < rhs.displayName
517	                }
518	                return leftIndex < rightIndex
519	            }
520	        let nextOverallStatus = rollup(nextHosts)
521	        hosts = nextHosts
522	        overallStatus = nextOverallStatus
523	        logHostPhasesIfNeeded(nextHosts)
524	        logOverallStatusIfNeeded(nextOverallStatus)
525	    }

527	    private func snapshot(from record: HostRecord) -> HostConnectivitySnapshot {
528	        let observations = Array(record.observations.values)
529	        let routeDiagnostics = record.routeDiagnostics.values.sorted { $0.route < $1.route }
530	        let routePhase = phaseForRouteDiagnostics(routeDiagnostics)
531	        let observationPhase = rollupObservations(observations)
532	        return HostConnectivitySnapshot(
533	            id: record.id,
534	            displayName: record.displayName,
535	            endpoint: record.endpoint,
536	            phase: record.lifecyclePhase ?? routePhase ?? observationPhase,
537	            lastCheckedAt: latestDate(observations.compactMap(\.lastCheckedAt)),
538	            lastSuccessAt: latestDate(observations.compactMap(\.lastSuccessAt)),
539	            routeDiagnostics: routeDiagnostics
540	        )
541	    }

543	    private func phaseForRouteDiagnostics(_ diagnostics: [RouteDiagnosticSnapshot]) -> HostConnectivityPhase? {
544	        guard let failed = diagnostics.first(where: { $0.appCritical && $0.routeStatus == .failed }) else {
545	            return nil
546	        }
547	        return .partial("\(failed.route) failed")
548	    }
549	
550	    private func rollupObservations(_ observations: [Observation]) -> HostConnectivityPhase {
551	        guard let strongest = observations.min(by: {
552	            priority(for: $0.phase) < priority(for: $1.phase)
553	        }) else {
554	            return .unknown
555	        }
556	        return strongest.phase
557	    }
558	
559	    private func rollup(_ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot]) -> AppConnectivityOverallStatus {
560	        guard !hosts.isEmpty else {
561	            return bootstrapStatus ?? .unconfigured("No relay host configured.")
562	        }
563	
564	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
565	            if case .configurationError = $0.phase { return true }
566	            return false
567	        }) {
568	            return .configurationError(status.phase.message)
569	        }
570	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
571	            if case .backgrounded = $0.phase { return true }
572	            return false
573	        }) {
574	            return .backgrounded("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
575	        }
576	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
577	            if case .resuming = $0.phase { return true }
578	            return false
579	        }) {
580	            return .resuming("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
581	        }
582	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
583	            if case .reconnecting = $0.phase { return true }
584	            return false
585	        }) {
586	            return .reconnecting("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
587	        }
588	        if let status = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
589	            if case .stale = $0.phase { return true }
590	            return false
591	        }) {
592	            return .stale("\(status.displayName): \(status.phase.message)")
593	        }
594	        let onlineLikeCount = hosts.filter { $0.phase.isOnlineLike }.count
595	        let checkingCount = hosts.filter { status in
596	            if case .checking = status.phase {
597	                return true
598	            }
599	            return false
600	        }.count
601	        if checkingCount == hosts.count {
602	            return .checking(hosts.count == 1 ? hosts[0].phase.message : "Checking \(hosts.count) hosts")
603	        }
604	        if onlineLikeCount > 0, checkingCount > 0 {
605	            return .partial("Online \(onlineLikeCount)/\(hosts.count), checking \(checkingCount)")
606	        }
607	        if onlineLikeCount == hosts.count {
608	            if let partial = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
609	                if case .partial = $0.phase { return true }
610	                return false
611	            }) {
612	                return .partial("\(partial.displayName): \(partial.phase.message)")
613	            }
614	            return .online(hosts.count == 1 ? hosts[0].phase.message : "\(hosts.count) hosts online")
615	        }
616	        if onlineLikeCount > 0 {
617	            let failing = hosts.first { !$0.phase.isOnlineLike } ?? hosts[0]
618	            return .partial("\(failing.displayName): \(failing.phase.message)")
619	        }
620	
621	        if let error = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
622	            if case .error = $0.phase { return true }
623	            return false
624	        }) {
625	            return .error("\(error.displayName): \(error.phase.message)")
626	        }
627	        if let offline = firstStatus(hosts, matching: {
628	            if case .offline = $0.phase { return true }
629	            return false
630	        }) {
631	            return .offline("\(offline.displayName): \(offline.phase.message)")
632	        }
633	
634	        return .checking("Waiting for first check")
635	    }
636	
637	    private func priority(for phase: HostConnectivityPhase) -> Int {
638	        switch phase {
639	        case .configurationError:
640	            return 0
641	        case .backgrounded:
642	            return 1
643	        case .resuming:
644	            return 2
645	        case .reconnecting:
646	            return 3
647	        case .stale:
648	            return 4
649	        case .checking:
650	            return 5
651	        case .offline:
652	            return 6
653	        case .error:
654	            return 7
655	        case .partial:
656	            return 8
657	        case .online:
658	            return 9
659	        case .unknown:
660	            return 10
661	        }
662	    }
663	
664	    private func firstStatus(
665	        _ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot],
666	        matching predicate: (HostConnectivitySnapshot) -> Bool
667	    ) -> HostConnectivitySnapshot? {
668	        hosts.first(where: predicate)
669	    }
670	
671	    private func latestDate(_ dates: [Date]) -> Date? {
672	        dates.max()
673	    }
674	
675	    private func hostIndex(_ hostID: String) -> Int {
676	        hostOrder.firstIndex(of: hostID) ?? Int.max
677	    }
678	
679	    private func logHostPhasesIfNeeded(_ hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot]) {
680	        for host in hosts {
681	            guard lastLoggedHostPhases[host.id] != host.phase else {
682	                continue
683	            }
684	            lastLoggedHostPhases[host.id] = host.phase
685	            DockLog.connectivity.info("connectivity host phase host_id=\(host.id, privacy: .public) endpoint=\(host.endpoint, privacy: .public) phase=\(host.phase.logDescription, privacy: .public) message=\(DockLog.redacted(host.phase.message), privacy: .public)")
686	        }
687	    }

689	    private func logOverallStatusIfNeeded(_ status: AppConnectivityOverallStatus) {
690	        guard lastLoggedOverallStatus != status else {
691	            return
692	        }
693	        lastLoggedOverallStatus = status
694	        DockLog.connectivity.notice("connectivity overall status=\(status.label, privacy: .public) message=\(DockLog.redacted(status.message), privacy: .public)")
695	    }
696	}

9	    ) -> SystemHealthSnapshot {
10	        SystemHealthSnapshot(
11	            summary: overallStatus,
12	            categories: SystemHealthCategory.allCases.map { category in
13	                SystemHealthCategorySnapshot(
14	                    category: category,
15	                    status: status(for: category, hosts: hosts, overallStatus: overallStatus)
16	                )
17	            },
18	            hosts: hosts
19	        )

22	    private func status(
23	        for category: SystemHealthCategory,
24	        hosts: [HostConnectivitySnapshot],
25	        overallStatus: AppConnectivityOverallStatus
26	    ) -> SystemHealthCategoryStatus {
27	        if hosts.isEmpty {
28	            return .notChecked("No relay host is configured.")
29	        }
30	
31	        let routeNames = routeNames(for: category)
32	        let diagnostics = hosts.flatMap(\.routeDiagnostics).filter { routeNames.contains($0.route) }
33	        if diagnostics.isEmpty {
34	            return fallbackStatus(for: category, overallStatus: overallStatus)
35	        }
36	
37	        if let failed = diagnostics.first(where: { diagnostic in
38	            diagnostic.routeStatus == .failed || diagnostic.routeStatus == .blocked
39	        }) {
40	            return .failed(
41	                failed.statusReasons.first?.message ?? "\(category.title) is failing.",
42	                nextAction: "Run check or open host details."
43	            )
44	        }
45	
46	        if let degraded = diagnostics.first(where: { diagnostic in
47	            diagnostic.routeStatus == .degraded || diagnostic.routeStatus == .partial || diagnostic.routeStatus == .stale
48	        }) {
49	            return .degraded(
50	                degraded.statusReasons.first?.message ?? "\(category.title) has partial or stale evidence.",
51	                nextAction: "Run check or review technical details."
52	            )
53	        }
54	
55	        if diagnostics.contains(where: { $0.routeStatus == .healthy }) {
56	            return .healthy("\(category.title) route evidence is healthy.")
57	        }
58	
59	        return .notChecked("No completed check for \(category.title.lowercased()).")
60	    }
61	
62	    private func fallbackStatus(
63	        for category: SystemHealthCategory,
64	        overallStatus: AppConnectivityOverallStatus
65	    ) -> SystemHealthCategoryStatus {
66	        switch overallStatus {
67	        case .checking, .reconnecting, .resuming:
68	            return .checking("Checking relay health.")
69	        case .online:
70	            switch category {
71	            case .dockFeed:
72	                return .healthy("Dock feed is receiving app evidence.")
73	            case .diagnostics:
74	                return .healthy("Relay process is reachable.")
75	            case .threadDetail, .archive, .voice:
76	                return .notChecked("No recent \(category.title.lowercased()) evidence.")
77	            }
78	        case .partial(let message):
79	            return .degraded(message, nextAction: "Run check or open host details.")
80	        case .offline(let message), .error(let message), .configurationError(let message), .unconfigured(let message):
81	            return .failed(message, nextAction: "Open Relay Settings.")
82	        case .backgrounded(let message):
83	            return .stale(message, nextAction: "Bring the app foreground to refresh.")
84	        case .stale(let message):
85	            return .stale(message, nextAction: "Run check.")
86	        }
87	    }

90	        switch category {
91	        case .dockFeed:

93	        case .threadDetail:

private func rowPrecedesByRecency(_ lhs: DockRowViewModel, _ rhs: DockRowViewModel) -> Bool {
